Implementation and tests for story file validation are present and passing.
Key implementation files: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Top-level JSDoc explicitly ties this rule to the story: - "Rule to validate @story annotation references refer to existing story files" - @story docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION. - Core behavior: - Scans all comments in Program(), extracts lines starting with "@story" (handleComment, validateStoryPath) fulfilling REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION. - Delegates path validation to processStoryPath(), which: - Calls performSecurityValidations(...) (from helpers) to reject disallowed absolute paths and unsafe traversal (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Enforces .story.md extension when requireStoryExtension is true via hasValidExtension(storyPath), and reports messageId "invalidExtension" when invalid (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - Calls reportExistenceProblems(...) to check existence and boundaries. - reportExistenceProblems(...) uses normalizeStoryPath(...) to resolve candidates and existence info, then handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(...) to enforce project boundaries, and finally reportExistenceStatus(...) to: - Report "fileMissing" for missing files. - Report "fileAccessError" with detailed error info for fs-error results (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY). - Rule metadata: - meta.docs.description: "Validate that @story annotations reference existing .story.md files" (Core Functionality acceptance criterion). - meta.messages includes: - fileMissing: "Story file '{{path}}' not found" (clear message for missing files; User Experience). - invalidExtension: "Invalid story file extension for '{{path}}', expected '.story.md'". - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{path}}'". - fileAccessError: "Could not validate story file '{{path}}' due to a filesystem error: {{error}}. Please check file existence and permissions." (explicitly surfaces filesystem errors and guidance; REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, User Experience). - meta.schema defines options storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension, enabling REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS. - create(context): - Derives cwd from context.cwd if present, else process.cwd() as fallback, matching story guidance about project-root resolution using context.cwd (REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION). - Reads rule options (storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension) and defaults: - storyDirectories defaults to ["docs/stories", "stories"] (defaultStoryDirs) (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, Implementation Notes). - allowAbsolutePaths defaults to false; requireStoryExtension defaults to true, as required.
- src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - JSDoc ties utility layer to story 006.0, with @req tags for path resolution, existence, security, error handling, performance, project boundary. - Path resolution & existence: - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - If storyPath starts with "./" or "../", resolves against cwd only. - Otherwise, resolves first as cwd + storyPath, then for each configured storyDirectories entry resolves cwd + dir + basename(storyPath). - This implements REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION and REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, matching documented examples. - getStoryExistence(candidates): - Iterates candidates, using checkSingleCandidate() with in-memory cache Map fileExistStatusCache to avoid repeated fs operations (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION). - Returns status "exists" (with matchedPath), "missing", or "fs-error" with a representative error. This is used by normalizeStoryPath to feed rule decisions. - normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs) returns { candidates, exists, existence } and never throws; existence.status is used by reportExistenceStatus and handleProjectBoundaryForExistence (REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION). - Filesystem safety & error handling: - checkSingleCandidate(candidate): - Wraps fs.existsSync and fs.statSync calls in try/catch. - Distinguishes: - Non-existent or non-file paths → {status: "missing"}. - Regular files → {status: "exists"}. - Any thrown error → {status: "fs-error", error}. - Caches each result in fileExistStatusCache to avoid repeated IO. - This satisfies REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION. - __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests(): dedicated API used in tests to clear cache between scenarios (REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION, testability). - Security / extension helpers: - isAbsolutePath, containsPathTraversal, isTraversalUnsafe, hasValidExtension(".story.md"), isUnsafeStoryPath combine to support REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION and extension enforcement. - Project boundary enforcement: - enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd): - Normalizes cwd and candidate via path.resolve; - Ensures candidate is equal to cwd or under cwd prefix (normalizedCandidate.startsWith(normalizedCwd + path.sep)). - Returns {candidate, isWithinProject} (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY).
- src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - Contains helper utilities referenced from the main rule for project boundaries and security, all annotated to story 006.0. - analyzeCandidateBoundaries(candidates, cwd): - Uses enforceProjectBoundary on each candidate to compute whether there are any in-project or out-of-project candidates (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS). - handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(...): - If all candidates are out-of-project and none are in-project, calls reportInvalidPath(...) and returns true, short-circuiting further checks. - If existenceResult.status === "exists" but matchedPath is outside project boundary, also reports invalidPath. - This ensures misconfigured storyDirectories or absolute paths cannot validate files outside the project (REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS, REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION). - performSecurityValidations(...): - Rejects absolute paths when allowAbsolutePaths is false, via path.isAbsolute, reporting invalidPath and stopping processing. - For any path containing ".." or path separators, resolves against cwd and ensures result starts with cwd + path.sep; if not, reports invalidPath and returns false. - This adds another layer of security against traversal and out-of-project references (REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION).
- src/index.ts - Includes "valid-story-reference" in RULE_NAMES and in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES under key "traceability/valid-story-reference": "error". - This ensures the rule is exported and can be enabled via flat config, matching the story's configuration examples and Integration acceptance criterion.

traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION appear to be fully implemented and verified by tests.
- Core Functionality: The valid-story-reference ESLint rule validates @story annotations, ensuring they reference existing story files with the .story.md extension by default. It relies on normalizeStoryPath and storyExists to resolve candidates and check existence, reporting fileMissing and invalidExtension appropriately. - Quality Standards & Safety: Filesystem access uses synchronous fs APIs (appropriate for ESLint rules) wrapped in try/catch with a caching layer, never throwing errors to ESLint. Project boundary and path security are enforced via enforceProjectBoundary and performSecurityValidations. - Integration: The rule operates on annotations discovered in comment nodes and is registered in the plugin export and severity config, integrating with annotation format validation and the overall plugin structure. - User Experience: Clear, distinct error messages are defined for missing files, invalid extensions, invalid paths, and filesystem errors, and tests assert their usage and contents. - Error Handling: Dedicated tests mock fs errors (EACCES, EIO) to ensure storyExists and the rule properly handle permission and IO failures as non-throwing conditions and report fileAccessError diagnostics. - Documentation: The story file includes specification details, path resolution rules, configuration examples, and matches the behavior of the implemented code.
Given the presence of comprehensive rule implementation, supporting utilities, project-boundary/security helpers, and extensive Jest + RuleTester coverage directly referencing this story and its requirements, this story is assessed as fully implemented and passing.
